edges.notes: gcc/g++ invoke GNU as and GNU ld on typical GNU/Linux triplets.
GCC is a major production C and C++ compiler implementation.
Default relocatable and executable output uses ELF on typical Unix-class targets.
Debug builds with -g emit DWARF on typical ELF targets.
Linux kernel has historically been built with GCC; documentation references GCC.
GCC includes a RISC-V port among many backends.
Clang and GCC are substitutable C/C++ compilers on many Linux and cross-compile flows.
GCC -g debug builds on ELF targets supply DWARF and symbols for GDB.
GCC targets glibc on typical GNU/Linux triplets for C/C++ standard library linkage.
GCC is used to build musl-based Linux systems (e.g. Alpine) with musl as the C library.
g++ links and distributes GNU libstdc++ as the default C++ standard library implementation.
GCC toolchain packages are provided in Alpine repositories for builds on and for the distribution.
GCC is central to Debian build-essential and package build flows on the distribution.
GCC is central to Ubuntu build-essential and package build flows on the distribution.
GCC is central to Fedora development tool groups and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participates in RHEL developer toolsets and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participates in Rocky Linux developer tool groups and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participates in AlmaLinux developer tool groups and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participates in CentOS Stream developer tool groups and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participated in historical CentOS Linux developer tool groups and RPM package build flows on the distribution.
GCC participates in FreeBSD base and ports toolchains that link against FreeBSD libc.
GCC participates in OpenBSD base and ports toolchains that link against OpenBSD libc.
GCC participates in NetBSD base and pkgsrc toolchains that link against NetBSD libc.
GCC participates in DragonFly base and dports toolchains that link against DragonFly libc.
GCC participates in illumos distribution toolchains that link against illumos libc.
GCC may appear in legacy or third-party Android cross toolchains that link against Bionic when configured.
GCC commonly pairs with newlib in embedded and bare-metal cross-compilation toolchains.
